successors.name: Yue (state)
successors.text: Wu, 'absorbed' by Yue in 473; King Goujian of Yue 'destroyed and annexed Wu in 473, after which he was recognized as hegemon'

ledger.x: 12th century BC: Taibo founds Wu in the Yangtze delta (infobox 'Foundation by Taibo: 12th century BC').
584: Wu rebels against Chu and annexes the Chu city of Zhoulai.
506: King Helü invades Chu and Wu takes the Chu capital Ying.
505: Qin and Chu drive Wu out of Ying.
482: while Fuchai holds a conference, Yue takes Wu's capital.
473: the siege of the capital ends and Yue annexes Wu.
473: Yue absorbs Wu and King Goujian becomes hegemon.

wars.name: Wu's rebellion against Chu
wars.outcome: Wu 'defeated Chu for the first time and annexed the Chu city of Zhoulai'.

wars.name: Wu conquest of Xu
wars.outcome: King Helü conquered Xu and extinguished the state.

wars.name: Battle of Boju and the Wu occupation of Ying
wars.outcome: Wu, with Cai and Tang, took Ying in 506; Qin and Chu defeated Wu in 505 and King Zhao returned to Ying.

wars.name: Wu-Qi war (Ailing)
wars.outcome: Wu 'turned to other campaigns, defeating the State of Qi in 484 BC'; no border changed.

wars.name: Yue's conquest of Wu
wars.outcome: Yue captured the capital in 482 while Fuchai was at a conference; Wu could not recover and was absorbed in 473.

certainty.note: Wu's frontiers are city territories and marcher lands; the 6th-century conquests (Xu, Zhoulai, Ying) have no boundaries on the pages opened.
